text: Host 10.0.2.30 sends a DNS query of type NULL for a short name under pirate.sea to 10.0.2.20 on UDP port 53.
source_text: The client opened with a short check-in query for vaaaakardli.pirate.sea and the server answered within a millisecond.

text: 10.0.2.20 answers the check-in query with a DNS response to 10.0.2.30 in under a millisecond.
source_text: The client opened with a short check-in query for vaaaakardli.pirate.sea and the server answered within a millisecond.

text: 10.0.2.30 sends a DNS query whose first label is a 32-character random-looking string under pirate.sea.
source_text: The client then sent a query with a 32-character random-looking label to log in and receive the tunnel's network parameters.

text: 10.0.2.30 sends DNS test queries whose labels contain long runs of mixed-case letters, digits, accented characters and high-bit bytes.
source_text: Next came a series of "zi" test queries whose labels contain long runs of mixed-case letters, digits, accented characters and raw high-bit bytes; the server echoed each name back.

text: 10.0.2.20 returns a DNS response to each test query that echoes the queried name back to 10.0.2.30.
source_text: Next came a series of "zi" test queries whose labels contain long runs of mixed-case letters, digits, accented characters and raw high-bit bytes; the server echoed each name back.

text: 10.0.2.30 sends three short DNS queries under pirate.sea to select the encoding.
source_text: Three more short queries (sbhi1c, obsi1d, obli1e) selected the upstream and downstream codecs.

text: 10.0.2.30 sends DNS queries with long, high-entropy, binary-looking query names split across several labels to 10.0.2.20 on port 53.
source_text: Once the codecs were agreed, the client sent upstream data as long query names made of high-entropy, binary-looking labels split across several dot-separated segments.

text: 10.0.2.20 answers each data query with a DNS response carrying a payload in a NULL record back to 10.0.2.30.
source_text: Each of these queries was answered by a response that echoed the name and carried the downstream payload in the NULL record.

text: Between data bursts 10.0.2.30 sends short polling DNS queries under pirate.sea to 10.0.2.20.
source_text: Between data bursts the client kept polling with short queries such as paeacg2y.pirate.sea and paficihq.pirate.sea so the server could push data back at any time.

text: DNS queries from 10.0.2.30 arrive on average every 120 milliseconds with highly irregular spacing, from back-to-back bursts to pauses of several seconds.
source_text: Queries arrived on average every 120 milliseconds but very irregularly, from bursts of back-to-back queries to pauses of several seconds.

text: 10.0.2.30 sends 222 DNS queries totalling about 26 kB and receives 212 DNS responses totalling about 44 kB from 10.0.2.20.
source_text: The client sent 222 queries (about 26 kB) and received 212 responses (about 44 kB), so more data flowed from the server to the client than the other way around.

text: 10.0.2.30 and 10.0.2.20 exchange two ARP requests and two ARP replies.
source_text: All traffic stayed on the single pair 10.0.2.30 and 10.0.2.20; the only other packets were two ARP request/reply exchanges between the two hosts.
